title: Sparsification conjecture
formal:
Is every monadically stable class of finite simple undirected graphs structurally nowhere dense? Precisely, with the definitions below, prove or refute
\[
\forall\mathcal C\subseteq\mathfrak G\
\left[
\operatorname{MS}(\mathcal C)\Longrightarrow
\exists\mathcal D\subseteq\mathfrak G\ \exists T\
\left(
\operatorname{ND}(\mathcal D)\ \land\
\forall H\in\mathcal C\ \exists G\in\mathcal D\
H\in T(G)
\right)
\right].
\]
Here \(\mathfrak G\) is the set of finite simple undirected graphs up to isomorphism, \(\operatorname{MS}\) denotes monadic stability, \(\operatorname{ND}\) denotes nowhere denseness, and \(T\) is a single first-order transduction with finitely many unary colors and one vertex variable per output vertex.

The source class \(\mathcal D\), number of colors and formulas of \(T\) may depend on the whole target class \(\mathcal C\). They must be fixed for that class, independently of the size or identity of \(H\). The graph \(G\) and its coloring may depend on \(H\). The covering requirement is \(\mathcal C\subseteq T(\mathcal D)\); the transduction may also produce graphs outside \(\mathcal C\). Neither class is assumed closed under taking subgraphs or induced subgraphs, and neither is required to be decidable or effectively presented. This is an existence statement, with no time bound, bound on the size of a preimage, or algorithm for finding the preimage.
why: A resolution would determine whether a central model-theoretic restriction on definable order patterns has an exact structural explanation in terms of sparse graphs. A positive answer would identify all monadically stable classes as logical images of nowhere dense classes, unifying two major descriptions of graph structure. A negative answer would exhibit a form of monadic stability that every such sparse representation misses. The target is the existence of a uniform representation for an entire class, a distinct structural issue from algorithms for evaluating first-order sentences.
status_note: Open as Conjecture 15 in the CSL paper published 18 February 2026 and as Conjecture 2 in the LICS paper published 9 July 2026. A bounded primary-source review through 16 September 2026 found no verified proof or refutation of the unrestricted statement. The inspected 2026 results establish restricted cases, an almost nowhere dense representation, or different neighborhood-complexity and merge-width conclusions; none supplies the required nowhere dense source class for every monadically stable class. The audit checked actual PDF definitions and theorem scopes, not all theorem proofs, and is not an exhaustive bibliography or a Lean verification.

importance.reason: Individual assessment: a central universal representation conjecture connecting monadic stability in finite model theory with nowhere denseness in structural graph theory. It asks for an exact characterization of an extensive family containing both sparse and dense graph classes, rather than a decomposition for one restricted family. Either outcome would clarify the reach of logical representations by sparse graphs and a major organizing principle for the field. This assessment replaces the explicitly unassessed midpoint 50; it does not depend on venue, recency, or the existence of an open-question label.

sentences: Monadic stability means that no fixed first-order formula defines arbitrarily long orders in graphs of the class after arbitrary unary coloring.
The Sparsification Conjecture asks whether every such class can be obtained from a nowhere dense graph class by one fixed first-order transduction.
The transduction uses finitely many unary colors and vertex and edge formulas, while the sparse source class excludes a sufficiently large clique as a shallow minor at every fixed radius.

A resolution would decide whether this logical restriction on possibly dense graphs has an exact explanation through uniform sparse representations, beyond the restricted and almost nowhere dense cases already known.
A complete Lean answer must prove the representation for every monadically stable class or exhibit one such class that defeats every nowhere dense source class and every allowed transduction.

definitions:
Write \(\mathbb N_0=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\), \(\mathbb N_{\ge1}=\{1,2,\ldots\}\), and \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), where \([0]=\varnothing\). A finite simple undirected graph \(G\) has a finite vertex set \(V(G)\) and an irreflexive symmetric adjacency relation \(E_G\). Its isomorphism type can be represented by a graph on \([n]\), using \(n\) and its finite symmetric zero-diagonal adjacency matrix. Isomorphism means a bijection of vertices preserving adjacency. The set \(\mathfrak G\) consists of all such isomorphism types, including the empty graph. A graph class is an arbitrary subset of \(\mathfrak G\), and it can contain graphs of unbounded size. Statements about a graph or an output of a transduction are understood up to isomorphism. This representation fixes the finite objects without imposing a computability condition on a class.

For \(q\in\mathbb N_0\), a \(q\)-colored expansion \(G^+\) of \(G\) assigns an arbitrary subset \(P_i^{G^+}\subseteq V(G)\) to each of the unary predicates \(P_1,\ldots,P_q\). These subsets can overlap and can be empty. The adjacency relation remains \(E_G\). A first-order formula in this signature is a finite expression built from atoms \(x=y\), \(E(x,y)\), and \(P_i(x)\), using negation, conjunction and existential quantification of individual vertex variables. Other Boolean connectives and universal quantification are abbreviations. An assignment interprets variables as vertices; equality, adjacency and color atoms have the stated meanings, connectives have their usual Boolean meanings, and an existential quantifier ranges over all vertices of \(G\). There are no set quantifiers, additional binary relations, distinguished order, function symbols or constants. In particular, the labels in an adjacency-matrix representation are not a relation available to a formula.

The class \(\mathcal C\) is monadically stable, written \(\operatorname{MS}(\mathcal C)\), if the following uniform absence of definable orders holds. For every \(q\in\mathbb N_0\), every tuple length \(t\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\), and every first-order formula \(\psi(\bar x,\bar y)\) over the \(q\)-colored graph signature whose free variables lie in two disjoint lists \(\bar x,\bar y\) of length \(t\), there is \(L\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\) such that no graph \(G\in\mathcal C\), no \(q\)-colored expansion \(G^+\), and no sequence of tuples \(\bar a_1,\ldots,\bar a_L\in V(G)^t\) satisfies
\[
\forall i,j\in[L]\quad
\left(G^+\models\psi(\bar a_i,\bar a_j)
\ \Longleftrightarrow\ i\le j\right).
\]
Tuples need not have distinct coordinates, and coordinates in different tuples can overlap. The bound \(L\) may depend on \(\mathcal C,q,t,\psi\), but must work for all graphs in the class and all interpretations of the colors. No computable dependence is required. Formulas used here need not be symmetric. The prohibition concerns orders definable by every fixed formula after arbitrary unary coloring, not just orders visible directly in the adjacency relation.

A first-order transduction \(T\) in this card is a finite triple \((q,\delta(x),\varphi(x,y))\), where \(q\in\mathbb N_0\) and the two formulas are over the \(q\)-colored graph signature, with free variables among those displayed. For each colored expansion \(G^+\), it produces the simple undirected graph with vertex set
\[
W=\{v\in V(G):G^+\models\delta(v)\}
\]
and adjacency, for \(u,v\in W\), given by
\[
u\ne v\quad\land\quad
\bigl(G^+\models\varphi(u,v)\ \lor\
G^+\models\varphi(v,u)\bigr).
\]
Define \(T(G)\) to contain every graph obtainable by varying all \(q\) unary predicates, up to isomorphism, and put
\[
T(\mathcal D)=\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal D}T(G).
\]
Both formulas are evaluated in the entire colored input graph before the domain restriction to \(W\). An arbitrary choice of retained vertices can be expressed by an additional unary color in \(\delta\). No new vertices are created: this is the noncopying convention of the source. In particular, the domain does not consist of tuples of vertices and is not factored by a definable equivalence relation. The tuple variables in the definition of monadic stability do not change this one-dimensional transduction convention.

Equivalently, the source defines monadic stability by requiring that no such fixed transduction from \(\mathcal C\) produces all half-graphs. The half-graph \(H_\ell\), for \(\ell\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\), has distinct vertices \(a_1,\ldots,a_\ell,b_1,\ldots,b_\ell\), no edges within either displayed side, and an edge \(a_i b_j\) exactly when \(i\le j\). Thus the source's equivalent condition is
\[
\forall T\ \exists\ell\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\quad H_\ell\notin T(\mathcal C).
\]
The no-order definition above fixes the predicate \(\operatorname{MS}\) used in the formal statement; this equivalent half-graph description connects it to the source formulation.

For \(r\in\mathbb N_0\) and \(s\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\), the complete graph \(K_s\) is a depth-\(r\) minor of \(G\) if there are pairwise disjoint nonempty vertex sets \(B_1,\ldots,B_s\subseteq V(G)\) and centers \(c_i\in B_i\) such that every vertex in \(B_i\) can be joined to \(c_i\) by a path of at most \(r\) edges lying entirely in \(G[B_i]\), and for each distinct \(i,j\) there is an edge of \(G\) with one endpoint in \(B_i\) and the other in \(B_j\). Here \(G[B_i]\) is the induced graph on \(B_i\); a length-zero path is allowed. Additional edges within or between the branch sets are allowed. This is the shallow-minor condition obtained by contracting disjoint connected subgraphs of radius at most \(r\).

The class \(\mathcal D\) is nowhere dense, written \(\operatorname{ND}(\mathcal D)\), when
\[
\forall r\in\mathbb N_0\ \exists s\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\
\forall G\in\mathcal D\quad
K_s\text{ is not a depth-}r\text{ minor of }G.
\]
The excluded size \(s\) may depend on \(\mathcal D\) and \(r\), but not on \(G\). No computable function giving \(s\) is required. A class \(\mathcal C\) is structurally nowhere dense if some nowhere dense \(\mathcal D\) and one transduction \(T\) satisfy \(\mathcal C\subseteq T(\mathcal D)\), exactly as in the formal statement.
answer_criterion:
Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the formal assertion, or of its full logical negation, with the finite graph universe, monadic stability, depth-\(r\) minor relation and transduction semantics defined above.

A positive answer must provide the existential nowhere dense source class and a single finite transduction for every monadically stable target class, with all the stated quantifier dependencies. It must prove that every target graph has some colored preimage in that source class. Neither an effective assignment of source classes and formulas nor an algorithm for finding preimages is an additional requirement.

A negative answer must establish
\[
\exists\mathcal C\subseteq\mathfrak G\
\left[
\operatorname{MS}(\mathcal C)\ \land\
\forall\mathcal D\subseteq\mathfrak G\ \forall T\
\left(
\operatorname{ND}(\mathcal D)\Longrightarrow
\exists H\in\mathcal C\ \forall G\in\mathcal D\
H\notin T(G)
\right)
\right].
\]
Thus it must prove monadic stability of one whole graph class and rule out every nowhere dense source class and every fixed finite transduction for that class. The graph \(H\) witnessing failure may depend on \(\mathcal D,T\), and nonmembership in \(T(G)\) excludes every allowed coloring of \(G\). Failure of one particular representation, a result limited to a subclass of monadically stable classes, or a representation with a weaker sparsity property does not establish either required conclusion. This is an exact yes/no assertion; the numerical \(1/100\) tolerance does not relax its quantifiers or structural conditions.

context_blocks.text: Ossona de Mendez states the conjecture directly in his 2021 STACS account. The CSL 2026 source repeats it as Conjecture 15, separately from that paper's questions about strongly flip-flat classes. This card retains the unrestricted monadically stable target.

The source uses unary colors and first-order domain and adjacency formulas without copying vertices. This card keeps that convention. Some presentations also allow a fixed number of copies before coloring; Pilipczuk explains why allowing those copies does not change transducibility from the sparse classes under consideration, including nowhere dense classes. Allowing tuple domains of unrestricted fixed dimension would be a different convention.

The LICS 2026 paper states the same general conjecture and records established cases involving bounded shrub-depth, linear clique-width, clique-width, twin-width and merge-width. Its new results impose additional restrictions and use existential positive transductions; they do not assert the unrestricted representation asked for here.

Dreier, Gajarský and Pilipczuk give a representation of every monadically stable class by an almost nowhere dense class in their January 2026 preprint. They explicitly distinguish almost nowhere denseness from nowhere denseness for arbitrary graph classes. That weaker conclusion does not resolve this conjecture.

The bounded review also checked a July 2026 preprint on neighborhood complexity and radius-one merge-width in monadically dependent classes. Its stated conclusions concern different structural properties and do not give the nowhere dense source class required here.

Read the actual CSL 2026 publisher PDF, Section 2 definitions pp. 41:4–41:7 and Section 4 Conjecture 15 p. 41:12. Publisher metadata states 18 February 2026. Conjectures 2 and 16 concern stronger flip-flatness conditions and are not substituted. The source uses fixed unary colors and formulas delta(x), phi(x,y), symmetrizes phi by disjunction with its reversal, and deletes self-loops. It has no copying operation.

Read the actual STACS 2021 publisher PDF, Section 3 pp. 2:3–2:4 and Conjecture 3.1. Its formula-plus-arbitrary-domain-restriction presentation has the same class-level expressive power as the CSL formula-pair presentation, because a fresh unary color can select the output domain. The 2021 publication predates the imported 2026 occurrence; the source year remains preserved in provenance.

Read arXiv2501.04166v1, 7 January 2025, relevant definitions and copying discussion printed pp. 8–12/PDF10–14 and Section 4.2.2 printed pp. 53–54/PDF55–56. The relevant number in this inspected edition is Conjecture 3, not the different numbering shown by some search indexes. The copying discussion says transducibility agrees for source-class properties closed under Cartesian product with a fixed clique, and explicitly covers the survey's relevant statements. The draft therefore fixes the CSL noncopying convention rather than leaving finite copying unspecified.

For that optional copying convention, the survey first takes a fixed finite number c of disjoint copies, adds a binary copy relation linking copies of the same original vertex, and then colors and interprets. It explains the connection to a Cartesian product with K_c and why this does not change transducibility from nowhere dense classes. This optional operation is not an implicit operation of T in the draft. General tuple domains or definable quotients are not allowed.

Read both the actual January 2026 arXiv2601.15890v1 PDF and the later 25-page LICS publisher PDF. Publisher metadata states 9 July 2026. The latter has Conjecture 2 and Theorem 4 pp. 67:3–67:4, Theorem 10 p. 67:5, and the original tuple-order definition with common tuple length and one sequence of tuples at p. 67:7. These differ from the preprint numbering. Its loop/reflexivity and co-matching assumptions belong to the existential-positive strengthening, not to the ordinary simple-graph conjecture retained here.

The draft's monadic-stability predicate follows LICS p. 67:7 exactly: every fixed formula over finitely many unary predicates, equal positive tuple lengths, no arbitrarily long sequence on which its truth agrees with i <= j. Explicit bounds and color quantifiers are the negation of that order property. Constants are unnecessary because singleton colors can name parameters. It also gives the CSL half-graph formulation as a sourced equivalence, without defining stability by edge half-graphs alone.

Read arXiv2601.14906v1, submitted 21 January 2026, relevant introduction and Appendix A.1–A.2 pp. 28–29. Definition 37 and the following paragraph explicitly say almost nowhere denseness need not imply nowhere denseness on arbitrary classes. Theorem 41 has an almost nowhere dense source and an efficient interpretation. Its existence and running-time claim therefore do not settle the exact ND source requirement. No complete independent proof audit of Theorem 41 is claimed.

Read arXiv2607.10941v1, 12 July 2026, actual PDF abstract, introduction and main theorem statements pp. 1–4. Theorems 2 and 4–5 concern neighborhood complexity and radius-one merge-width for monadically dependent classes. They are not an unrestricted sparsification theorem with a nowhere dense source; neither a stronger model-checking conjecture nor a merge-width characterization is substituted for this card.

Search indexes were only discovery aids; definitions, conjectures and theorem scopes were checked in actual primary PDFs. No verified resolution was found. This does not certify exhaustive current openness or all proofs in the papers.

A scan of active cards for monadic stability/structural nowhere density located TCS-6678, whose canonical record was read; it asks for deterministic FPT first-order model checking on hereditary effectively monadically dependent classes, a different mathematical target. Existing inactive related links can remain as provenance and are suppressed by publication. No exact reviewed active duplicate was found.

The formulation quantifies over arbitrary sets of finite isomorphism types, no class encoding or membership algorithm. For each target class one fixed source class, fixed finite formulas and fixed color count suffice; individual preimages and colorings vary with the target graph. The source need not be hereditary. The full negation quantifies universally over every source class and transduction and permits a different missing target graph for each pair. An absent finite witness for the whole class is not a formulation defect.

The positive result must establish exact structural existence; no source-size bound, effective source selection, fixed-point logical extension, integer approximation, auxiliary milestone or proposed proof technique appears in the mathematical target. The five-sentence summary and public significance concern the structural classification, not a claim that monadically stable model checking remains unresolved.
